old: [A man] whose inheritance and family are depleted; of small income; whose statements of country, caste, lineage, name and work are contrary; of concealed livelihood and work; addicted to meat, liquor, delicacies, food, scents, garlands, clothes and ornaments; who spends excessively; addicted to unchaste women, gambling and liquor-dealers; who often lives abroad; who goes to unknown places; who moves about in secluded spots, forests, gardens and at wrong times; who holds many consultations in a hidden place or a place with meat; who has secret treatment given to fresh wounds; who is always indoors; who approaches [others]; who is devoted to a woman; who often asks about others' possessions, others' women, goods and houses; who is in contact with despised work, treatises and implements; who moves at night in the shade of covering walls; who sells misshapen articles at the wrong place and time; in whom hostile intent has arisen; of low work and birth; who conceals his form; who is an āliṅgin by a mark, or a mark-bearer (liṅgin) of different conduct; with deeds done earlier (apadāna); pointed out by his own deeds; who hides on seeing the nāgarika and the high officials, slinks away, sits without breath, is agitated, with dry and altered voice, face and colour; who is frightened at the approach of men with weapons in hand: one should suspect [him to be] one or another of those who live by violence, theft, misappropriation of treasure-troves and deposits, para-prayoga, or secrecy. — Such is seizure by suspicion.
